title: Settle Duration.to_iso8601/1 on a negative component
description:
The single call the audit left open. to_iso8601/1 raises a %TypeDB.Error{} for
a negative months/days/nanos rather than emitting "P-1Y-2M", which its own
parse/1 rejects and which TypeDB misparses as a type label. The alternatives
are returning {:error, reason} - a signature change, so it must happen before
1.0 or never - or normalising silently.

Only reachable from a hand-built struct; TypeDB never sends a negative
duration. Low stakes, but the signature is frozen at 1.0, so the decision is
not deferrable.

title: Hide internal modules from the published docs
description:
TypeDB.Wire, TypeDB.Bang, TypeDB.Transport and TypeDB.Token are implementation
detail. Rendered on hexdocs they read as public surface, and after 1.0 someone
will depend on them. @moduledoc false, or an explicit "internal, no stability
guarantee" note for the ones worth reading.

title: Add an API snapshot test
description:
SemVer is currently a promise kept by attention. Render every public module,
function, arity and spec into a checked-in snapshot file and fail the build when
the two disagree. Changing the API then requires changing the snapshot in the
same commit, which is exactly the moment to ask whether it is a minor or a
major.

The machinery already exists: test/typedb/api_convention_test.exs uses
Code.Typespec.fetch_specs/1 and spec_to_quoted/2 to walk the surface.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot committed; a deliberate signature change fails the suite with a readable diff; CONTRIBUTING explains how to update it and how to classify the change.

title: Add operation-level telemetry spans
description:
lib/typedb/telemetry.ex:10 is explicit: one span per HTTP request, including
each retry and each renew-and-retry. So [:typedb, :request, :stop] counts
attempts, not queries. A dashboard built on it cannot answer how long a query
took end to end, how many queries the application ran, or what fraction needed
a retry - the three questions anyone actually asks.

Add [:typedb, :query, :start|:stop|:exception] and [:typedb, :transaction, ...]
around the whole logical operation, with the per-attempt spans nested inside
and unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: New spans documented in TypeDB.Telemetry with their metadata; existing :request spans unchanged; a test asserts one operation span per query regardless of the number of attempts.

title: Cap the backoff delay with :retry_max_delay
description:
Exponential growth is unbounded. With the documented default base and
max_retries: 10, the last sleep is over 50 seconds - inside the caller process,
holding whatever that process holds. Nothing in the config can currently stop
it.

Add :retry_max_delay (default in the low single-digit seconds), applied after
jitter, validated by Config.parse_timeout/3 like every other timeout.

title: Bound the total time of a request, not just each attempt
description:
Today :timeout means one attempt. The worst case a caller actually
experiences is timeout * (max_retries + 1) + the sum of the backoffs. A caller
that writes timeout: 5_000 and reads the docs still gets a call that can block
for well over half a minute, and there is no option that says otherwise.

This is the item that must land before 1.0 whatever the answer, because both
candidate answers change the meaning of an existing documented option:
  (a) add :deadline as a wall-clock budget, each attempt getting min(:timeout,
      remaining) - additive, two knobs to explain;
  (b) redefine :timeout as the budget for the whole operation and derive the
      per-attempt timeout - one knob, but a silent behaviour change for anyone
      already relying on the current meaning.

Decide, write down why, then implement.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in the issue; option implemented and validated; a test proves a request cannot exceed the budget across retries; TypeDB moduledoc states the worst case arithmetic explicitly.

title: Add jitter to the default backoff
description:
lib/typedb/config.ex:238 returns trunc(base * 2^(attempt-1)) exactly. Every
caller that fails at the same instant - which is what a server restart, a
network blip or a rolling deploy produces - waits exactly the same number of
milliseconds and retries in lockstep, repeatedly, for as many attempts as
:max_retries allows. That is the textbook thundering herd, and it makes the
driver an amplifier of the outage it is trying to ride out.

Full jitter (sleep a uniform random value in [0, delay]) is the default in the
AWS SDKs, Finch, Tesla and Oban for the same reason. Determinism stays
available through the existing :retry_backoff function form, which tests
already use.
acceptance_criteria: Default backoff is jittered; a test asserts the spread over many attempts rather than a fixed value; the function form of :retry_backoff is still honoured verbatim; TypeDB moduledoc documents the default.

title: Observability: telemetry spans and logging that survive production
description:
Telemetry today is one span per HTTP attempt and five Logger call sites across
four modules. You can measure attempts; you cannot measure operations, you
cannot see a give-up, and you cannot turn any of it down without touching the
host application Logger config.

title: Freeze the public API for 1.0
description:
1.0.0 is a promise about the surface, so the surface has to be deliberate and
mechanically defended. Includes the one judgement call the audit left open.

title: Retry, timeout and backoff semantics fit for production
description:
1.0.0 freezes defaults, and every item here IS a default. Changing any of them
afterwards is a major bump, so they have to be right before the tag.

The driver retries inside the caller process (lib/typedb/transport.ex:126-158)
with a pure exponential backoff (lib/typedb/config.ex:238) and no jitter, no
cap, and no overall deadline. That is fine on a laptop and wrong under load.

title: Write an honest Limitations section
description:
Things a user will otherwise discover the hard way: answers are decoded whole,
so there is no streaming or pagination and a large match is a large term; a
connection points at one server with no failover; mix typedb.check needs a
POSIX shell; one Finch pool per connection; retries are blocking and happen in
the caller process.

None of these are bugs. All of them are surprises.

title: Write the guides
Add a fault-injecting HTTP adapter for tests
description:
The transport containment (lib/typedb/transport.ex contain/3) promises that no
adapter fault escapes as a bare exception. That promise is currently tested
with a handful of hand-written adapters.

Build one adapter that can be told to truncate the body, return malformed JSON,
answer with the wrong content type, return a 5xx storm, stall past the timeout,
raise, exit and throw - then assert across the whole public API that every
single one comes back as a %TypeDB.Error{}.
acceptance_criteria: Every public function is exercised against every fault mode; no fault produces an exception other than %TypeDB.Error{}; no fault kills the connection process.

title: Property-based round-trip tests for the wire boundary
description:
Duration, DateTimeTZ, Given.encode_rows/1 and Concept.cast/2 are the pure
functions where TypeDB wire format meets Elixir types, and they are where the
subtle bugs have actually been: silent loss of the raw duration string,
NaiveDateTime precision changing under a round trip, decimals rendered with a
TypeQL suffix.

Example-based tests find the cases you thought of. StreamData finds the
nanosecond that rounds, the offset at the boundary, the string with the quote.

title: Matrix the optional dependencies
description:
The one bug that reached hex was a %Finch.Response{} struct pattern that made
the package fail to compile for anyone without finch - invisible to a matrix
that varied only Elixir and OTP. The same shape of bug is waiting in the
decimal and jason paths.

Add jobs: no optional deps at all; decimal present; jason present and JSON
absent. Compile and run the suite in each.
acceptance_criteria: A build with zero optional dependencies compiles and passes; removing the guard from any optional-dependency code path fails that job.

title: Nightly run against the latest TypeDB release
description:
A scheduled workflow against TypeDB latest so that a server release breaks our
build before it breaks somebody application. Failure notifies rather than
blocks.

title: Run the integration suite against more than one TypeDB version
description:
README says TypeDB 3.x. CI proves 3.12.1. Pick the oldest 3.x release the
driver claims and add it to the matrix alongside the newest - or narrow the
claim in the README to what is actually tested. Both are honest; the current
state is not.

title: Decide the shape of Transaction.analyze/3
description:
analyze/3 returns TypeDB raw map, unmodelled and unversioned. Either give it a
struct like every other answer, or state in the docs that it is passed through
verbatim and tracks the server rather than this driver SemVer. It should be one
of those on purpose, not by omission.

title: Add ConceptRow.to_struct/2
description:
lib/typedb/concept_row.ex:96 spends an entire paragraph warning that
Kernel.struct/2 on a string-keyed map silently returns a struct full of nils,
and then shows the four-line incantation that avoids it. That paragraph is a
feature request with extra steps. Ship the safe version.

title: Make the raise-vs-return rule uniform across the public API
description:
TypeDB.query/4 raises ArgumentError for an unknown :transaction_type
(lib/typedb.ex:178). Transaction.open/4 raises FunctionClauseError for the same
mistake. Config.new/1 returns {:error, %TypeDB.Error{kind: :config}}. Three
answers to one question.

Pick the rule - programmer error raises, runtime input returns - write it in
CONTRIBUTING, then make the code and the api_convention test enforce it.

title: Pin the real server error codes for every operation
description:
The unit suite asserts the codes the stub returns, and the audit already found
four places where the stub had invented codes the server does not use (M9,
M9b - a single made-up USR2 standing in for SRV4, USU4 and USD3). Four found by
looking at one endpoint is evidence about the endpoints nobody looked at.

Enumerate the failure of every operation against a live server, record the code
and status, and assert them in the integration suite so the stub can be checked
against reality instead of trusted.

title: Add TypeDB.Error.retryable?/1
description:
Callers who want their own retry loop currently have to write
kind in [:transport, :timeout], which is driver internals copied into user
code - and it goes stale the moment A4 makes some :server errors retryable.
One predicate, owned by the driver, tested against every kind.

title: Add a :log_level connection option
description:
Five Logger call sites, three levels, four modules, and no way for an
application to quieten the driver short of filtering the global Logger by
module. A library that cannot be turned down gets turned off.

Add :log_level (default matching current behaviour, :none accepted) and one
table in the docs listing every line the driver can emit, at what level, with
what metadata.

title: Raise the level of the failures that currently whisper
description:
Retry exhaustion logs nothing. A failed token renewal logs nothing. Both are
production incidents in miniature and both should be :warning. The retry
attempts themselves stay at :debug - they are noise until they are not.

title: Emit an event when retries are exhausted
description:
Giving up after :max_retries is currently invisible: the caller gets an
ordinary error, indistinguishable from a first-attempt failure, and the only
trace that the driver tried five times is a Logger.debug that nobody has
enabled. Retry exhaustion is a signal that something upstream is broken and it
should be countable.

title: Ship TypeDB.Telemetry.attach_default_logger/1
description:
Finch, Ecto, Oban and Broadway all ship one, because the gap between "the
driver emits telemetry" and "I can see what my app is doing" is otherwise an
afternoon of handler plumbing per project. One function, a documented log
level, off by default.

title: Narrow retry eligibility from HTTP method to operation
description:
lib/typedb/transport.ex:122 decides idempotence by method: GET and DELETE
retry, everything else does not. That is safe but blunt. POST
/v1/transactions/open is perfectly safe to retry, and so is a read-only
/v1/query - both are currently one-shot, so a single dropped packet fails a
query the driver could have transparently recovered.

Meanwhile commit must never be retried and correctly is not. Move the decision
to the call sites that know the semantics, keeping the method rule as the
default for anything that does not say.

title: Retry retryable HTTP statuses and honour Retry-After
description:
lib/typedb/transport.ex:127 retries only kind :transport and :timeout. A
TypeDB behind a proxy, an ingress or a load balancer answers 502/503/504 while
it restarts, and 429 when it is shedding load. None of those is retried, so the
driver gives up instantly on exactly the failures that retrying was built for.

Add a configurable retryable-status set (429, 502, 503, 504 by default) and
honour a Retry-After header when present, clamped by :retry_max_delay.

title: Documentation a stranger can start from
description:
Reference docs are complete (every public function has a moduledoc and specs).
What is missing is the narrative layer and an honest statement of limits.

title: Test depth: properties, fault injection, soak
description:
349 unit tests across three adapters is good coverage of the paths we thought
of. The bugs that got through were in the paths we did not: precision loss on a
round trip, an optional dependency being absent, a stub disagreeing with the
server. Those three classes each have a mechanical answer.

title: Compatibility matrix and CI hardening
description:
README claims TypeDB 3.x; CI proves 3.12.1. Either widen the proof or narrow
the claim. Also: the one bug that reached hex (a %Finch.Response{} struct
pattern in an optional-dependency code path) was invisible to a CI matrix that
only varied Elixir and OTP.

title: Error taxonomy, containment and predicates
description:
Every failure is supposed to be a %TypeDB.Error{} with a stable :kind and
TypeDB code. Two things are unfinished: public functions that still raise
ArgumentError/FunctionClauseError for bad input, and the absence of any
predicate telling a caller whether an error is worth retrying.

title: Commit the benchmarks the CHANGELOG quotes
description:
The CHANGELOG publishes ~1900 req/s for Finch against 77 for httpc at 200-way
concurrency. Those scripts live in a scratch directory that no longer exists.
Numbers in a changelog that nobody can reproduce are decoration; put them under
bench/ and re-run them for the 1.0 notes.

title: Resolve Decimal once, not per value
description:
lib/typedb/concept.ex:240 calls Code.ensure_loaded?(Decimal) for every decimal
attribute cast. It is cheap and it is cached, and it is still a lookup on the
hot path of a query that returns ten thousand rows. Resolve it at compile time
or once per connection.

title: Decide whether 1.0 supports multiple servers
description:
TypeDB.Server.servers/1 returns cluster membership. Nothing consumes it. A
connection has one :url.

For TypeDB CE that is correct and complete. For anyone running more than one
node it means the driver has no answer for a node going away, and they will
find that out during an incident.

The decision is in or out. If out, say so in the Limitations section (G2) and
close this. If in, H2 follows.

title: Review the ex_doc module groups
description:
Once the internals are hidden, the remaining grouping should be re-read as a
table of contents rather than a list of files.

title: Publish a Livebook
description:
Mix.install, a local TypeDB in Docker, schema, insert, match, transactions. It
is the fastest way for someone to find out whether this driver fits, and it is
worth a Run in Livebook badge on the README.

title: Set a coverage floor
description:
Coverage is measured and never enforced. Set the floor at the current number
so it can only go up.

title: Put a bounded concurrency soak in CI
description:
The 200-way burst and the token-expiry-straddling transactions were run by
hand during the audit and their results are quoted in the CHANGELOG. A bounded
version belongs in the integration job so the claim keeps being true.

title: Compile and unit-test on Windows
description:
mix typedb.check needs a POSIX shell by decision, and that is written down.
The driver itself is pure Elixir and should be proven to work on Windows rather
than assumed to.

title: Cache the dialyzer PLT
description: Minutes per run, every run, for a cache key that is just the lock file.

title: Write the versioning policy
description:
What 1.0 covers: public function signatures, error kinds and codes, telemetry
event names and metadata keys, the config option set, the transport behaviour.
What it does not: internal modules, the exact text of messages, TypeDB own wire
format. Without this written down, every bug fix is arguably a breaking change.

title: Make Exception.message/1 consistently useful
description:
A %TypeDB.Error{} carries kind, code, status, message and reason but the
rendered message does not always include the request that produced it. When
this lands in a log line or an exit reason it should say what was attempted.

title: Put :database and :transaction_id in request metadata
description:
lib/typedb/transport.ex:163 builds metadata of connection, method, path and
attempt. Grouping metrics by database - the first thing anyone does on a
multi-tenant server - means regex-parsing :path. Both values are known at the
call site.

title: Document the latency arithmetic
description:
Once A1-A4 land, the TypeDB moduledoc should state, in one short table, what a
call can cost in the worst case for the default configuration. Right now a
reader has to derive it from three separate options.

title: Cluster and availability: decide in or out for 1.0
description:
TypeDB.Server.servers/1 returns the cluster membership and nothing in the
driver uses it. A single connection points at a single URL. This is either a
1.0 feature or a documented non-feature; drifting is the only bad answer.

title: Performance: keep the numbers honest and the hot path clean
description:
The CHANGELOG publishes throughput numbers that live only in a scratch
directory, and the value-casting path calls Code.ensure_loaded?/1 per value.

title: Write a release checklist
description:
Tag, CI gate, hex publish, docs, CHANGELOG, GitHub release. It ran off memory
and a rewritten workflow file for 0.1.0. Write it down before the second
release proves memory does not scale.

title: Set the repository topics and homepage
description:
Needs a human with repo admin - no MCP tool in the agent session exposes
repository settings.

  gh repo edit NoeticEcho/TypedbEx --homepage "https://hexdocs.pm/typedb" \
    --add-topic elixir --add-topic typedb --add-topic database \
    --add-topic driver --add-topic graph-database --add-topic typeql

Purely findability.

title: Document the beads workflow in CONTRIBUTING
description:
A contributor cloning the repo finds a .beads directory and no explanation.
Cover: install bd, bd init --from-jsonl to seed from the committed export until
the Dolt remote exists, bd ready to find work, bd update --claim, and the
convention of naming the issue id in the commit message so bd doctor can spot
orphans.
close_reason: Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md: install, bd ready, claim/close, seeding a fresh clone, and that issues.jsonl is an export rather than the source of truth.

title: Implement multi-address connections with failover
description:
Only if H1 says in. Accept :urls, health-check members, fail over on
:transport errors, refresh membership from /v1/servers. Substantial: it touches
config validation, the connection state machine and every retry decision, and
it needs a multi-node integration environment to test honestly.

title: Release housekeeping
description: Small, mostly outside the code, mostly needing a human.
